assessment.nobel_worthiness: Establishes liquid-liquid phase separation and condensate formation as a general physical-chemical principle of intracellular organisation, a new concept of molecular organisation without membranes. It brings polymer physics, thermodynamics and phase behaviour into cell biology and has reoriented work on P granules, nucleoli, stress granules and disease-linked aggregation, including links to amyloid-type states. Original, conceptually clear and broadly consequential.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne made the founding observation of liquid-like P granules and the quantitative framing; Rosen's multivalent-interaction work supplied the in vitro, mechanistic and thermodynamic basis. Pappu and Mittag made strong sequence-encoded and physics-based contributions, so the three-person limit forces a hard choice; my selection is a judgement, not a verified settlement of credit.
assessment.maturity: Roughly a decade of independent confirmation across many labs and systems, and the concept is widely used. Debate persists about which cellular condensates are true equilibrium phases and how functionally important they are, but the core phenomenon is robust and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Ongoing dispute over the physiological relevance and exact phase-thermodynamic status of some reported condensates.
Fair division of credit among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag; I am relying on memory of the literature, not verification.
Whether the committee regards this as chemistry or as cell biology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are lipid self-assembly and phase behaviour turned into a delivery technology: pH-dependent charge, lipid packing and non-bilayer phases control encapsulation and endosomal release. Their central role in siRNA therapeutics and in mRNA vaccines gives very large, demonstrated impact on top of the physical-chemical design principles.
assessment.attribution: Cullis's group built the lipid-nanoparticle formulation and ionizable-lipid concept; Anderson and Langer drove combinatorial lipid discovery and delivery of RNA payloads. MacLachlan, Hope and Madden made important formulation contributions. Credit is spread across academic and industrial groups, and the 2023 Physiology or Medicine prize on mRNA modification may complicate the framing.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at global scale, and confirmed independently by multiple formulations and products. Timely, with mechanistic understanding still developing.
uncertainties: Attribution across academic and industrial inventors is contested and I cannot verify the precise priority record.
Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize may make the committee see this as already partly recognised.
Which of the several lipid-chemistry contributors is decisive is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape and funnel theory recast protein folding as statistical thermodynamics on a rugged but biased landscape, resolving Levinthal's paradox and giving a general physical-chemical language for folding, binding and misfolding. It is a concept-level contribution that unifies theory and experiment and connects to aggregation and amyloid.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes, Onuchic and Bryngelson established the funnel and landscape formalism; Dill contributed the hydrophobic-collapse and lattice-model picture; Fersht supplied experimental phi-value analysis. A three-person prize leaves out either the experimental or the theoretical side, which is a real tension.
assessment.maturity: Several decades of confirmation through experiment and simulation. Recognition has been slow rather than premature, and the 2024 prize for structure prediction and design may have partly covered the area.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 Chemistry prize for protein structure prediction and design.
Whether the concept is seen as foundational or as a conceptual framework rather than a discovery.
Allocation between theorists and Fersht's experiments.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one base into another on DNA without double-strand cleavage, using deaminase chemistry on a programmable scaffold. A very important chemistry-driven genome-engineering tool, already in clinical trials and therapy development.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the conceptual and experimental development; Komor (cytosine base editor) and Gaudelli (adenine base editor) did the decisive experimental work in his lab. Kondo and Nishida made a related, independently developed cytidine-deaminase approach, so credit is not fully settled.
assessment.maturity: Rapid independent adoption and clinical validation. Timely but still maturing, and long-term safety and off-target profiles remain under study.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize and with prime editing (B051) which shares a principal inventor.
Whether to include Kondo and Nishida over the trainee co-discoverers.
I am not able to independently verify clinical outcome data.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation uses small molecules to induce proximity between a target and an E3 ligase, changing what is considered druggable. Molecular glues such as thalidomide analogues and the PROTAC concept are new chemical modes of action with growing clinical trial activity.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies were early in the PROTAC concept and its development; Ciulli contributed structure-guided design and VHL ligands; Handa, Ito and others identified cereblon as the thalidomide target. Gray and others developed degrader chemistry. Credit is broadly distributed and the one-to-three constraint omits important figures.
assessment.maturity: Clinical translation is advancing but no approved PROTAC drug is established in my knowledge; the mechanistic base is well confirmed. Possibly slightly early.
uncertainties: Whether recognition would be premature absent an approved degrader drug.
Split between the PROTAC concept and the cereblon molecular-glue mechanism.
Many credited names; I am uncertain about relative priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA origami demonstrated that long single strands can be folded by staples into arbitrary two- and three-dimensional shapes, a clear and general demonstration of programmed molecular self-assembly. It has enabled new nanoscale devices, templates and biophysical tools.
assessment.attribution: Rothemund introduced scaffolded DNA origami; Yan and Shih extended it to three dimensions and to functional structures. Seeman, the founder of structural DNA nanotechnology, is not among the credited names, which weakens any fair configuration from this list.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and widely reproduced for two decades, with application impact still developing relative to the concept.
uncertainties: The foundational contribution of structural DNA nanotechnology by a person not in the credited names, so attribution cannot be complete.
Real-world application impact is still modest compared with the concept.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native mass spectrometry measures intact non-covalent protein complexes, including membrane proteins and their lipid interactions, in the gas phase with preserved stoichiometry and sometimes topology. It supplies unique physical-chemical information on assembly, binding and lipid-protein interplay.
assessment.attribution: Robinson extended it to large and membrane complexes; Heck contributed instrumentation and applications; Chait and Loo made early contributions. Credit is spread among several comparably central groups.
assessment.maturity: Mature, widely adopted and independently confirmed; however, how faithfully gas-phase measurements reflect solution structure remains discussed.
uncertainties: Crowded field of analytical-chemistry candidates, including proteomics mass spectrometry (B030), with an unclear order of merit.
Fidelity of gas-phase structure to solution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Self-assembled monolayers and soft lithography gave molecular-level control of interfaces and a general route to patterning, grounded in surface chemistry and amphiphile self-organisation. They underpin much of surface science, biosensing and microfluidics.
assessment.attribution: Whitesides led soft lithography and the broad adoption of thiol-on-gold monolayers; Nuzzo and Allara reported the early alkanethiol-on-gold monolayer work; Sagiv's earlier silane monolayers are a priority question. Whitesides is clearly central but the other credit is genuinely contestable.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation and broad use; recognition is long delayed rather than premature, though some of the field has moved on.
uncertainties: Priority between Sagiv, Nuzzo and Allara and the thiol-on-gold work.
Whether the committee sees it as a technique cluster rather than a single discovery.
